overview: Multiple alleles means many versions of one gene; polygenic inheritance means many genes controlling one trait.
genZNote: Multiple alleles: one gene, several costume options. Polygenic: several genes teaming up for one look.

aspects.label: Number of Genes Involved
aspects.valueA: One gene, but with more than two allele variants in the population.
aspects.valueB: Two or more genes, each contributing a small additive effect to one trait.

aspects.label: Alleles per Individual
aspects.valueA: An individual still carries only two of the many possible alleles.
aspects.valueB: An individual carries multiple gene pairs, all influencing the same trait together.

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: ABO blood group system (IA, IB, i alleles).
aspects.valueB: Human skin colour and height, which show continuous variation.

aspects.label: Phenotype Pattern
aspects.valueA: Can still show discrete phenotype classes (A, B, AB, O).
aspects.valueB: Produces continuous, bell-curve variation rather than discrete classes.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: ABO blood grouping is the textbook example of multiple alleles with codominance (IA and IB) and recessiveness (i).
overlay.memoryTrick: Multiple alleles = many flavours of one gene. Polygenic = many genes, one trait.
overlay.commonMisconception: Multiple alleles existing in a population does not mean one person carries more than two — every diploid individual still has just two.
